The patrol and firefighting team dumped a rope bag to pull the boy ashore. After preliminary assessment by firefighting, the boy suffered minor injuries. He was taken to an ambulance for medical examination and treatment. There was no danger to his life. The police also assisted in contacting his family. The Coast Guard of the Northern Department of the Maritime Commission was reported to the First Shore Patrol at 1:00 p.m., and was dispatched to the scene. It was found that the boy was floating and sinking in the sea on the outside of the reef, and the situation was critical. After rescuers urgently tossed the rope bag, the boy clung to the rope, and the crowd quickly pulled to the shore. Due to the steep and slippery topography of the reef, the patrol and the consumer worked together again.
